summary.text: The contact email printed on your official site sits on a domain you use, and its registration runs out — after that, every enquiry sent to it bounces.
Your public rating is strong, yet none of the newest reviews on that profile carries a reply from you, so a homeowner comparing installers reads silence as indifference.
Your contractor grade differs between your own site and a public directory, so a tender panel caps the contract value it thinks you can take.

titles.c1: Two different main phone numbers are in public use, so callers reach different lines with no idea which is sales.

titles.n1: A public contractor profile may carry placeholder phone details, worth checking before a panel relies on it.
titles.n2: A revenue figure on your site is not repeated anywhere outside, worth checking how it reads to a buyer.
titles.n3: One listed office carries no street address, worth checking that customers can find and reach it.
titles.n4: Several of your newest reviews carry the same date, worth watching even though it proves nothing alone.
